q-81400.problem:

Express the compound statement above in symbolic form given the following:

- $P:10\text{ is divisible by }3$

- $Q:10\text{ is divisible by }4$
q-81400.worked_solution:
The given sentence is the negation of the following sentence: 

$10$ is divisible by $3$ or $4$, 

which can be expressed symbolically as $P∨Q.$

The negation is represented by the symbol "$¬$". 

Therefore, the given sentence is expressed symbolically as $¬(P∨Q).$

q-182350.name: Question 4
q-182350.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
q-182350.worked_solution:
First, we add a column for $¬B,$ where the truth values are opposite to the corresponding values in the column for $B.$ 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Then, we add a column for $A∧¬B.$ Remember that $A∧¬B$ is true if both $A$ and $¬B$ are true.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬B\,$ | $\,A∧¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |

q-182392.name: Question 5
q-182392.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
q-182392.worked_solution:
First, we add a column for $A∧B.$ Remember that $A∧B$ is true if both $A$ and $B$ are true.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Then, we add a column for $¬(A∧B).$ Remember that the truth values of $¬(A∧B)$ are opposite those of $A∧B.$

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
